Diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles; a square is a parallelogram, so this is verifying a parallelogram-family property -> LO-30, not the goal.
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal - LO-30 verbatim, not LO-29's angle sum.

Only one right angle fits in a triangle because the three angles total 180 degrees; that is the angle sum property LO-29 rests on, extended to the triangle.
All angles of a regular polygon are equal - the definition of regularity, not a computation, so goal-level rather than LO-29.
Polygons with diagonals partly outside are concave; a classification of polygons, which no LO covers -> goal-level.
Definition of a polygon (duplicate of qid:113505); definitional -> goal-level.
Bisectors of two adjacent parallelogram angles meet at 90 degrees because those angles are supplementary; a parallelogram property proved by reasoning -> LO-30.
Blind 'which is not true' MCQ, options absent from the row; goal-level rather than guessing between LO-29 and LO-30.
